# provision_server

[← Command index](README.md)

Take a server entry from nothing to deployed, hardened and verified.

## Synopsis

```
provision_server [options]
```

## Description

Runs every step of setting up a server from `[UserData.Servers]` in `~/JoyBox.ini`,
from this machine over SSH. The same stages run against a real host and against the
local test guest; each one checks what is already done, so running it again resumes
after a failure rather than starting over.

Stages, in order:

- `vm`: only when the entry names a test guest (`server_<n>_vm`). Builds it with
  `testvm`'s defaults at the entry's address, or starts it; waits for first boot and
  snapshots it as `provision-fresh`; points the domain and its subdomains at it in
  `/etc/hosts`.
- `login`: if the account cannot log in with the entry's key, logs in as root with
  that key, creates the account with root's authorised keys, and sets its password
  from `server_<n>_pass` when there is one.
- `day0`: copies `Bootstrap/scripts` and `Bootstrap/managers` from this checkout and
  runs, as root, the sudoers, docker, nginx and htpasswd setup, then the Storage Box
  mount when `server_<n>_storage_user` and `_host` are set, or local storage when
  not. Skipped once root login is closed.
- `deploy`: the same as `bootstrap.py -a setup -t remote_ubuntu -s <n>`, for
  `--components` or every component. Trusts mkcert's local authority first when the
  entry uses `tls_mode = mkcert`.
- `sshd`: proves the account's key login, snapshots a test guest as `pre-sshd`, runs
  the sshd hardening that closes root and password login, then proves the key login
  again. A test guest that loses it is reverted.
- `verify`: the `verify_server` checks, as the account.

Secrets come from the entry, so they can be `op://` references: `_htpasswd_pass` for
the admin pages, `_storage_pass` for the Storage Box, and `_pass` for the account.
They reach the server as files only root can read, and are removed after use.

## Options

### General

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-s, --server <server>` | Index of the server entry under `[UserData.Servers]`. |
| `-c, --components <components>` | Components to deploy; every remote component when omitted. |
| `--stages <stages>` | Stages to run, from `vm`, `login`, `day0`, `deploy`, `sshd` and `verify`; all of them when omitted. |

### Common options

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-v, --verbose` | Enable verbose mode. |
| `-p, --pretend_run` | Do a pretend run with no permanent changes. |
| `-x, --exit_on_failure` | Enable exit on failure mode. |
| `--no-preview` | Skip the preview confirmation prompt. |

## Examples

### Provision the local test guest in server entry 1

```bash
provision_server --server 1
```

### Provision a real server with only some components

```bash
provision_server -s 0 --components nginx certbot wordpress fitlog
```

### Redeploy and re-verify without the earlier stages

```bash
provision_server -s 1 --stages deploy verify
```

### Show what would run

```bash
provision_server -s 1 -p
```

## Notes

- Needs paramiko on this machine; `python3 bootstrap.py -a setup -t local_ubuntu --components python` installs it.
- A real host must accept root with the entry's key on first contact, as a freshly ordered server does when given that key.
- Root login is closed by the `sshd` stage, so on a hardened server the `login` and `day0` stages only confirm the account and move on.
- The exit code is 0 on success, the number of failed checks when only `verify` fails, and 1 when an earlier stage fails.
